query: What do players think of the story and characters in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33?
draft_reference_summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 stands out for its emotionally gripping narrative, strong characters and memorable world-building. Its writing remains a strength even where the pacing slows in the middle before picking up again.

draft_claims.text: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 stands out for its emotionally gripping narrative, strong characters and memorable world-building.
draft_claims.text_zh: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 的吸引力在于富有感染力的叙事、鲜明的角色和令人难忘的世界塑造。

supporting_evidence.quote:
✅ Pros: Emotionally gripping narrative with deep themes, innovative turn-based combat with real-time parry/dodge mechanics, breathtaking Surrealist & Belle Époque art direction, phenomenal soundtrack and top-tier voice acting.
❌ Cons: Strict combat timing requirements can feel exhausting for some, linear world exploration with limited traversal options, lack of a minimap and minor visual lip-sync bugs.
🏆Rating: 8.8 / 10

Chrono trigger WAS my favorite game of all time. I play and enjoy every genre of gaming. FPS, Metroidvanias, Rogue lites, Platformers and so on. Expedition 33 did everything that Chrono trigger didn't, and was just as innovative. Absolute perfection. Story, Writing, Voice Acting, Pacing, Gameplay, Graphics, Soundtrack... ALL 10's.

Imagine playing an incredibly fun and challenging game, and reading the greatest book, and watching the best movie... all at the SAME TIME. Brain broken. You owe it to yourself to play this one through.

Expedition 33 was an amazing experience from start to finish. The story, music, visuals and combat are all fantastic, and it's one of those games that sticks with you long after you finish it. Definitely worth playing.

- Soundtrack is phenomenal
- Story is incredibly well written, although slightly stagnates in the middle but then picks up again
- Characters are intriguing and well-designed
- Exploration is somewhat rewarding
- Combat is serviceable, with decent enemy variety, nothing groundbreaking but not bad either

The story, characters and soundtrack heavily carries the game.

8/10

Those who love turn based combat and little bit of difficulty, soundtracks are really good and world building is beautiful, I usually like fromsoftware art direction but here they did a good job.
I am looking forward to future "Clair Obscur:" titles

query: How is the soundtrack in Hollow Knight?
draft_reference_summary: Hollow Knight's hauntingly beautiful soundtrack is closely tied to its atmosphere: Christopher Larkin's music complements Hallownest's ruins and the melancholy of its forgotten kingdom.

draft_claims.text: Hollow Knight's hauntingly beautiful soundtrack is closely tied to its atmosphere: Christopher Larkin's music complements Hallownest's ruins and the melancholy of its forgotten kingdom.

supporting_evidence.quote:
Hollow Knight is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Its deeply immersive worldbuilding and masterful storytelling come together to create an unforgettable narrative. The phenomenal soundtrack also deserves every bit of praise it receives. Christopher Larkin was truly cooking, and many tracks have found their way into my everyday playlists.
The gameplay is equally impressive. Many boss fights feel like a dance as you weave in attacks and spells while dodging each strike. Having 100%ed this game and explored every corner of its world, I can’t recommend it highly enough to anyone looking for a rewarding time sink.

Hollow Knight is an amazing game with beautiful artstyle, phenomenal soundtrack and very very deep lore, but sometimes it can be difficult.
It is probably the best purchase in my life and is worth recommending.
Also GAME IS FILLED WITH BUGS.

Absolute Masterpiece! (9/10)
​Hollow Knight is a breathtaking journey through a beautifully dark and tragic world. Everything in this game comes together perfectly to create an unforgettable experience:
​Gameplay & Combat: Silky-smooth mechanics, tight controls, and rewarding progression.
​Music & Atmosphere: The soundtrack and visual design are hauntingly beautiful, drawing you deep into the lore of Hallownest.
​Challenge: The difficulty is tough and demanding, but incredibly satisfying to master.
​Final Score: 9 / 10
The only reason it’s not a full 10/10 is the lack of official Arabic lauage support. Other than that, it is near perfection. Highly recommended to anyone who loves Metroidvanias and great storytelling!

Hollow Knight is not just a game; it is a descent into a haunting, melancholic dream.

Team Cherry didn't just build a world; they unearthed a vast, forgotten kingdom. Hallownest is a masterclass in atmospheric storytelling, where every rain-soaked ruin in the City of Tears and every shadow in Deepnest echoes with lost glory, backed by Christopher Larkin’s achingly gorgeous score.

The gameplay is surgical perfection. Tight, responsive controls, the hypnotic satisfaction of nail-pogoing, and boss fights that demand absolute respect and rhythm. You get lost, you adapt, you overcome.

An untouchable monument of the Metroidvania genre and an absolute work of art. 10/10.

It has a amazing story, so lore deap charicters, and its amazing as a bullet easy to hell 2d platformer and great backtrack/areas, good sound tracks, and nice boss fights. also replayable with a charm (loadout) sistem. one thing... speedrun achivement.

Honestly, after waiting for what felt like forever, stepping into Pharloom as Hornet was worth every single second. I’m definitely not the most skilled gamer out there I died way more times than I’d like to admit but Hollow Knight: Silksong is an absolute masterpiece.

The movement feels so fluid and acrobatic compared to the original. Jumping, sprinting, and using Hornet’s needle craft makes combat feel like a fast-paced dance. The handcrafted art style, atmospheric music, and intricate world design continually blew me away. Every new area had me completely immersed, even when a brutal boss had me stuck for an hour.

It’s tough, but every victory feels earned and ridiculously satisfying. If you enjoy action platformers, atmospheric worlds, or just a really solid challenge, I can't recommend this game enough. Do yourself a favor and give it a play you won't regret it!

The game can be frustrating at the beginning because it is punishing, but it is still fair. I've also heard that there were bugs when it came out but they were all fixed by the time I started the game.

query: How do reviewers rate the narrative of Red Dead Redemption 2?
draft_reference_summary: Red Dead Redemption 2's narrative is highly praised for its writing, characters and atmosphere, with an emotional impact strong enough to move players to tears and leave a lasting impression.

draft_claims.text: Red Dead Redemption 2's narrative is highly praised for its writing, characters and atmosphere, with an emotional impact strong enough to move players to tears and leave a lasting impression.
draft_claims.text_zh: Red Dead Redemption 2 的剧情因出色的写作、角色和氛围受到高度评价，其情感感染力不仅令人印象深刻，也带来了感动落泪的体验。

supporting_evidence.quote:
I don't think RDR2 should be approached like most games. If I'm being honest, some of the gameplay is garbage. The horse controls can be annoying and there's no shortage of bugs. But you're not here for game mechanics. You're here for the delivery of a masterfully written story that uses a video game as its vessel.

This game affected me on a spiritual level. At two points in the story, I teared up and had to go on a walk to process thoughts that this game's story and characters invoked. It does a great job exploring masculine traits and the concept of "the end justifies the means". Combined with the beautiful, detailed environments and exceptional soundtrack, RDR2 is truly a work of art.

10/10 One of the best gaming experiences I’ve ever had.

Red Dead Redemption 2 is honestly on another level. The open world is absolutely incredible every place feels alive, every little detail feels intentional, and there’s always something new to discover. The story, characters, music, atmosphere, everything comes together so perfectly.

query: How does the combat feel in Hades II?
draft_reference_summary: Hades II's combat feels tight and satisfying, combining an enjoyable flow with more tactical decisions and expressive abilities; its changes are also praised as improvements over the first game.

draft_claims.text: Hades II's combat feels tight and satisfying, combining an enjoyable flow with more tactical decisions and expressive abilities; its changes are also praised as improvements over the first game.
draft_claims.text_zh: Hades II 的战斗紧凑、爽快，流畅的节奏与更具战术性的选择、丰富的能力表现结合在一起，也被认为比前作有所进步。

supporting_evidence.quote:
don't hate me for this, but I didn't like the first Hades.
HOWEVER Hades II has totally won me over and blown me away.
It hat tight satisfying combat, it's charming, the music is amazing, i like the unlock systems, is has a fishing minigame (this alone should sell you on this game)

Two years ago there was a low depressive period of my life where playing Hades II was the only habit and source of stability I could afford. It cradled me, gave enough comfort so I rested and recharged.

500 hours in I'm still in love, devoted, surprised with the game
I love art direction
I love all the little environment details
I love writing
I love voice acting
I love how combat flows

10/10, my perfect comfort game
thank you 💙

After playing Hades I had high expectations for the second game, and I must say that it delivered. The devs expanded on all ideas from the original and made it into a nice package with great combat, awesome soundtrack and really likable (and not) characters.
Definitely gonna put in quite a few hours into this game (so far beaten the main boss twice).

The original Hades is the most complete game that I have ever played.
While Hades II does not quite live up to that, with weaker characters, story, and worldbuilding, Supergiant has improved on the already great combat system and the power system. The enemy variety has increased, and the art is even more beautiful.

They basically made Hades again, but sacrificed some of the character and story depth for making the gameplay even more addictive. As good if not better than the original.

I remember loading up this game for the first time and feeling disappointed with the magic system since I thought it would take away from the gameplay's adrenaline. In fact it just make the gameplay feel more tactical; there are immediately twice as many layers and possibilities for builds. Which is only made better by having two distinct paths for progression!

There's not much to say about the audio-visual pieces, since the art and music are iterated from the original Hades and are similarly awesome. But yeah this game is great, and you will not regret playing it (I don't think you need to play the original but it definitely helps!)

Hades was a masterwork I don't even knwo how to call Hades II. Keeps the soul of the first game and gives everything everyone that loves Hades would want and more. More expressive skillset and gameplay, music and characters are enjoyable and memorable. A truly all around perfect game for the hack and slash genre.

supporting_evidence.quote:
Honestly, after waiting for what felt like forever, stepping into Pharloom as Hornet was worth every single second. I’m definitely not the most skilled gamer out there I died way more times than I’d like to admit but Hollow Knight: Silksong is an absolute masterpiece.

The movement feels so fluid and acrobatic compared to the original. Jumping, sprinting, and using Hornet’s needle craft makes combat feel like a fast-paced dance. The handcrafted art style, atmospheric music, and intricate world design continually blew me away. Every new area had me completely immersed, even when a brutal boss had me stuck for an hour.

It’s tough, but every victory feels earned and ridiculously satisfying. If you enjoy action platformers, atmospheric worlds, or just a really solid challenge, I can't recommend this game enough. Do yourself a favor and give it a play you won't regret it!

This game is amazing as a sequel, been waiting over 3 years for it, even participated in the silkposting. My favorite fight definetly was Karmelita with all the Lace fights as a close second, I enjoyed this game very much and i cannot wait for Sea of Sorrow.

As someone who is really passionate about Hollow Knight (Reached to the top of P5), this game felt natural. The bosses were not too difficult since I am used to the movement and seeing openings etc. But I can see a person completely new to hollow knight suffer with the past faced gameplay and double heart damage. I would really suggest playing Hollow Knight first and then picking this game up. If u already beat Hollow Knight, this game is a must play.

query: What do longtime fans think of the gameplay changes in Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War III?
draft_reference_summary: Compared with earlier Dawn of War games, Dawn of War III draws criticism for MOBA-like maps, smaller battles and the effort of managing heroes and creeps, leaving its mixture of designs unsatisfying. Base-building fares better in one comparison, improving on Dawn of War II while remaining less substantial than the original game.

draft_claims.text: Compared with earlier Dawn of War games, Dawn of War III draws criticism for MOBA-like maps, smaller battles and the effort of managing heroes and creeps, leaving its mixture of designs unsatisfying.
draft_claims.text_zh: 与系列前作相比，Dawn of War III 的 MOBA 式地图、缩小的战斗规模，以及同时管理英雄和小兵的负担，是玩法变化中最受批评的部分。

supporting_evidence.quote:
I will dig in my heels & defend the voice acting, music & art style. It's a 5/5 on atmosphere, it is a true WH40K game. But at the end of the day, gameplay rules with an iron fist & trying to merge the 2 previous games constitutions was poorly executed, if it was possible in the first place.

If you want good feels, this knocked it out of the park. But if you want a good game? only if you're ok with overpaying...

Played the campaign. Played a bunch of skirmish matches. Got wrecked in Multiplayer.

Things I like:
- Animations and graphics
- Unit abilities
- There is some basic base building

Things I didn't like:
- No horde survival mode
- Small scale battles for a 40k title
- Maps feel like they were trying to make this into a MOBA
- Really wanted all races, even if it was DLC

Bottom line... I reinstalled DOW Soulstorm, added the Ultimate apocalypse mod and carried on from there. Much better.

With 40K Dawn of War IV coming around the corner we must all agree that making a RTS-MOBA is not the play, having to supply creeps and balance heroes IS too much work especially since you have to macro the heroes and control the creeps with no option to automate or give up your hero slots or commander position

so do your best CIA impression and DENY EVERYTHING

What is, a Dawn of War III? We have no ties to such a title and we will not accept this SLANDER

0/9

draft_claims.text: Base-building fares better in one comparison, improving on Dawn of War II while remaining less substantial than the original game.
draft_claims.text_zh: 基地建设则有相对积极的评价：比 Dawn of War II 有进步，但仍不如初代完整。

supporting_evidence.quote:
I like it, rating it 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐. A lot busier than the other Dawn of War titles. Feels like you're commanding an actual big army this time. Also base-building is improved compared to Dawn of War 2, but still not as robust as OG Dawn of War. Audio and voice overs are great too. Makes you feel the urgency.

Also the power scaling of hero units, plus the tower system during skirmishes gives it a MOBA vibe. Makes it harder to zerg rush, which ngl in the earlier Dawn of War series is doable in some scenarios.

Not 5 star because of the cluttered UI. It takes some getting used to but needlessly complicated.

draft_reference_summary: Resident Evil Requiem's visuals are a clear strength in these accounts, with impressive graphics that can still look good at low settings.

draft_claims.text: Resident Evil Requiem's visuals are a clear strength in these accounts, with impressive graphics that can still look good at low settings.

supporting_evidence.quote:
10/10 – An absolute masterpiece.

Easily one of the best survival horror games ever made. The story keeps you hooked from start to finish, the atmosphere is peak tension, and the graphics are unbelievable—especially on an OLED display with ray tracing. It runs silky smooth at 100+ FPS, gunplay feels phenomenal, and the climax delivers in every way possible.

Capcom knocked it out of the park. If you love Resident Evil, this is an essential buy.

One of the best resident evil games I've played, up there with 2 and 4, which are my other favourites. Love the swapping between characters throughout, the 2 styles compliment each other really well. Graphics are amazing. It has some of the best acting in a game I have ever seen. Definitely deserves some awards I think.

Good old Resident Evil. Fantastic gameplay and an amazing story. Also great optimization and good looking graphics even on low settings and completed on the pc specs attached to my review. All in all from a 10/10 MUST PLAY!!!

Resident Evil Requiem is a great game. I'm a new Resident Evil player and loved playing through it. The gameplay and the mechanics were so good. I should finish Resident Evil 2 now since I still haven't finished it...
It also is greatly optimized in my opinion. I don't have a great pc and it still played very amazingly.
10/10

Another W for Capcom, a successful entry to the Resident Evil Franchise. Resident Evil Requiem combines mechanics from previous RE entries for Leon and Grace's gameplay and a nostalgic approach as we revisit Racoon City. 10/10 to me, need more dad jokes tho.

Good old Resident Evil. Fantastic gameplay and an amazing story. Also great optimization and good looking graphics even on low settings and completed on the pc specs attached to my review. All in all from a 10/10 MUST PLAY!!!

Well done Capcom!! The RE Engine gets better with every Resident Evil. Liking Grace she really sales the terror of horror. Angela Sant'Albano voice actress for Grace Ashcroft did an outstanding job capturing the paralyzing fear with in the Rhodes Hill Chronic Care Center. Gameplay gets better with each installment as well.It is a slightly reboot in my opinion.

It plays smoothly on Single player. Have yet to have the priviledge of a Multiplayer game but im not that patient either. The lore is nice and the creatures I've seen so far are on point. It's a nice addition to the resident evil series only true complaint is it never came to console.

Resident Evil Resistance is a really promising concept ! Taking the asymmetrical multiplayer idea of Dead by Daylight and putting it in the Resident Evil universe was such a cool move! The atmosphere, characters, and setting fit perfectly with this kind of gameplay.

...

That said, there are some downsides that really hurt the experience : long waiting times to find a match, a pretty limited map selection ; and maybe less of a dealbreaker but still noticeable : unbalanced teams. It can make matches feel a bit... chaotic, to say the least.

Easily the best Resident Evil game in the franchise. The combat, variety of play, and enemy types put it above both the original Resident Evil 4 and its Remake. The tension in the game blows Resident evil 2 Remake out of the water. I have no idea why CAPCOM stop funding this game. It's literally the only good Resident Evil game.

Just when I thought the Resident Evil series was dead, CAPCOM showed up to slap the taste out my mouth. Everything from the gameplay, the suspense, the tension, the horror, the survival, the story, the acting, the music, all of it is just on another level. It's like they read my mind and gave me the exact Resident Evil game I've been pining for since Resident Evil 4.

Turn the lights off, crank the volume up and take the ride, because Resident Evil is back with a vengeance.

query: PAYDAY 3 heist gameplay
draft_reference_summary: PAYDAY 3's heists benefit from satisfying gunplay and improved stealth, with later changes making the game more enjoyable. The weakness is staying power: highly upvoted criticism points to limited content and shallow heist variety that become repetitive after repeated clears. The skill trees also feel dull despite the stronger moment-to-moment play.

draft_claims.text: PAYDAY 3's heists benefit from satisfying gunplay and improved stealth, with later changes making the game more enjoyable.
draft_claims.text_zh: PAYDAY 3 的劫案体验受益于扎实的射击手感和改进后的潜行，后续调整也提升了游玩乐趣。

supporting_evidence.quote: Payday 3 has improved a lot since launch. The gunplay feels good, stealth is fun, and the developers keep adding new content and updates. It still has room to grow, but it's definitely worth playing with friends if you enjoy co-op heist games.

Credit where credit is due because Payday 3 has had such a turnaround from when it released.

It brings all the adrenaline and edge of your seat action of Payday 2 with EXTREMELY satisfying gunplay. It looks beautiful, it runs well, it's polished, the difficulty is rewarding, the music is brilliant, stealth is miles above PD2 in terms of complexity. And the talents and level reworks they've been doing have hit the sweet spot.

It feels unfair to compare the amount of content in this to its predecessor, when 2 has a solid 10 years worth of releases over Payday 3.

For a game that's been out nearly 3 years and had a rocky start, it's in a good place right now.

Genuinely quite good nowadays. Had a deservedly poor reputation when first released but after many revisions the game is actually quite a lot of fun now and worth picking up. The revised stealth mechanics alone make Payday 2 difficult to return to at times. Gunplay is much improved and all the new animations for interacting with drills, opening elevator shafts, etc. are neat touches. The game runs extremely well after the most recent engine upgrade and the upcoming crimebonds have some OK potential in exchange for free heists.

The skill trees are still quite boring unfortunately and there the main menu UI generally isn't great, particularly with the addition of crimebonds. Purchasing heist favours could do with being similar to Payday 2, rather than tucked away at the bottom of a vendor menu.

draft_claims.text: The weakness is staying power: highly upvoted criticism points to limited content and shallow heist variety that become repetitive after repeated clears.
draft_claims.text_zh: 不足主要在于持续游玩的吸引力：高赞评论批评内容有限、劫案变化不足，多次通关后容易重复。

supporting_evidence.quote:
I'm going to put as much effort into this review as Starbreeze does trying to save this game.

Was fun for the first 50 hours or so, not so much after that. Heist variation is shallow and doesn't feel good to complete after many clears. Music... subjective.

Overall, a severe side-downgrade from PAYDAY 2.

2. Lack of heist and content: Is the developer forget this game? Only 20 heist in total in this game.

Absolute Masterpiece! (9/10)
​Hollow Knight is a breathtaking journey through a beautifully dark and tragic world. Everything in this game comes together perfectly to create an unforgettable experience:
​Gameplay & Combat: Silky-smooth mechanics, tight controls, and rewarding progression.
​Music & Atmosphere: The soundtrack and visual design are hauntingly beautiful, drawing you deep into the lore of Hallownest.

Hollow Knight is not just a game; it is a descent into a haunting, melancholic dream.

Team Cherry didn't just build a world; they unearthed a vast, forgotten kingdom. Hallownest is a masterclass in atmospheric storytelling, where every rain-soaked ruin in the City of Tears and every shadow in Deepnest echoes with lost glory, backed by Christopher Larkin’s achingly gorgeous score.

The gameplay is surgical perfection. Tight, responsive controls, the hypnotic satisfaction of nail-pogoing, and boss fights that demand absolute respect and rhythm. You get lost, you adapt, you overcome.

An untouchable monument of the Metroidvania genre and an absolute work of art. 10/10.

supporting_evidence.quote:
Double Fine slapped a "1.0" sticker on this game and abandoned it. Whilst I appreciate that there are times that an Early Access game may not deliver all of the promised features, this game received a small fraction of those features proposed.

But this is a game review, not a review of Double Fine's business practices. So how is the game?

In short, the game is a mess of buggy AI with barely enough gameplay mechanics to sustain more than a couple of hours of play. The character morale system is horribly half-baked, and the game is little more than a series of repetitive busywork tasks.

That Double Fine now has it's greasy mitts out for Early Access funding for Massive Chalice barely a month after abandoning DF-9 is an insult to all of those people who put their faith in the company.

Never again.

Don't bother with this game. SBDF-9 a good concept and the game definitely had potential, but it's a flop.

- The game is (and feels) unfinished.
- Bugs and crashes are common even after "release".
- Poor user experience, frustrating character AI.
- As it was left by the developer, the game has a severe lack of depth.

I am extremely disappointed with the developer's choice of abandoning development, but I guess it's a risk one accepts when buying into Early Access.

Can't recommend.

Honestly, after waiting for what felt like forever, stepping into Pharloom as Hornet was worth every single second. I’m definitely not the most skilled gamer out there I died way more times than I’d like to admit but Hollow Knight: Silksong is an absolute masterpiece.

The movement feels so fluid and acrobatic compared to the original. Jumping, sprinting, and using Hornet’s needle craft makes combat feel like a fast-paced dance. The handcrafted art style, atmospheric music, and intricate world design continually blew me away. Every new area had me completely immersed, even when a brutal boss had me stuck for an hour.

It’s tough, but every victory feels earned and ridiculously satisfying. If you enjoy action platformers, atmospheric worlds, or just a really solid challenge, I can't recommend this game enough. Do yourself a favor and give it a play you won't regret it!

The gameplay is fun, albeit somewhat easy for people familiar with the mechanics, and the monster roster is very good. My biggest issues are that most high-level endgame gear is locked behind RNG mechanics that lack a sense of measurable progress which makes grinding feel pointless and the streamlining of out-of-hunt and exploration mechanics makes the gameplay less impactful because it feels like a constant race to the next combat encounter. Compared to the previous titles on PC, this one is fun, but feels like a downgrade in all the areas that give Monster Hunter it's identity.

A 4v1 asymmetrical multiplayer game where four teenagers with anime-tier special abilities attempt to escape an umbrella facility.

Meanwhile, the "Mastermind" controls the cameras, spawns zombies, and drops a literal 10-foot-tall Mr. X into a cramped hallway just to watch everyone panic-roll into walls.

RDR2 is a masterpiece in world-building, atmosphere, storytelling and immersion, which makes its controls all the more frustrating.

For a game so heavily focused on cinematic immersion, the clunky, sluggish and overly complicated controls constantly pull you out of the experience. Too many context-sensitive actions, too much input delay, too much fighting the character instead of simply controlling him.

It’s still an incredible game, but Rockstar’s refusal to properly adapt the controls for PC is a baffling design failure. Such a shame

This isn't Monster Hunter. It's Pokemon Snap. That isn't a hyperbole. You will spend 90% of this game on scripted rails listening to dialogue while you leave your controller on your desk. 5% running to the next NPC to start the next walk and talk section. And 5% actually Monster Hunter'ing.

Maybe it ends at High Rank, I haven't got there yet, but this is inexcusably horrible. "It Gets Good 15 Hours In!!!" isn't good game design. One of the worst games I've ever played coming out of one of my favorite series of all time.

Honestly, after waiting for what felt like forever, stepping into Pharloom as Hornet was worth every single second. I’m definitely not the most skilled gamer out there I died way more times than I’d like to admit but Hollow Knight: Silksong is an absolute masterpiece.

The movement feels so fluid and acrobatic compared to the original. Jumping, sprinting, and using Hornet’s needle craft makes combat feel like a fast-paced dance. The handcrafted art style, atmospheric music, and intricate world design continually blew me away. Every new area had me completely immersed, even when a brutal boss had me stuck for an hour.

It’s tough, but every victory feels earned and ridiculously satisfying. If you enjoy action platformers, atmospheric worlds, or just a really solid challenge, I can't recommend this game enough. Do yourself a favor and give it a play you won't regret it!

query: Are the graphics of Monster Hunter Wilds worth the performance cost?
draft_reference_summary: Monster Hunter Wilds' visuals do not have a consistently acceptable performance trade-off: attractive graphics coexist with smooth, crash-free play on some setups and reliance on frame generation on others. Around 50 FPS with balanced DLSS and no frame generation is considered acceptable in one account, though better performance is still wanted. Other feedback finds the performance poor and prefers Monster Hunter World's graphics and presentation.

draft_claims.text: Monster Hunter Wilds' visuals do not have a consistently acceptable performance trade-off: attractive graphics coexist with smooth, crash-free play on some setups and reliance on frame generation on others.

supporting_evidence.quote:
Wilds might be one of my top games of all time. Again I'm not a long time fan of the franchise, but from the games I have played, Wilds just feels like the most polished vision of Monster Hunter while working within the confines of the RE Engine.

Graphically, it's beautiful, and I'm very aware that I'm fortunate enough to have experienced the game after a year of patches and QoL changes, even now I have to use frame generation to sit comfortably in the triple digit FPS range.

Despite that, I really liked the story with the Guardian monsters, and just subtle elements like bows having infinite arrow coatings was really nice as a bow main. That said, wasn't a fan of the insect glaive's handling of the kinsect gauges.

Very excited for Ascendance.

supporting_evidence.quote:
Absolute Masterpiece! (9/10)
​Hollow Knight is a breathtaking journey through a beautifully dark and tragic world. Everything in this game comes together perfectly to create an unforgettable experience:
​Gameplay & Combat: Silky-smooth mechanics, tight controls, and rewarding progression.
​Music & Atmosphere: The soundtrack and visual design are hauntingly beautiful, drawing you deep into the lore of Hallownest.
​Challenge: The difficulty is tough and demanding, but incredibly satisfying to master.
​Final Score: 9 / 10
The only reason it’s not a full 10/10 is the lack of official Arabic lauage support. Other than that, it is near perfection. Highly recommended to anyone who loves Metroidvanias and great storytelling!

What a wonderful experience! The visuals, sound design, characters and gameplay are absolutely breathtaking. Went to the Resting Grounds many times just to listen to the music. Boss fights were all fun and unique from each other, platforming is intuitive, though quite challenging and frustrating in some places. As gloomy and melancholic the game is, it still offers quite a bit of color. Devastated I wont ever experience this game for the first time again.

✅ Pros: Emotionally gripping narrative with deep themes, innovative turn-based combat with real-time parry/dodge mechanics, breathtaking Surrealist & Belle Époque art direction, phenomenal soundtrack and top-tier voice acting.
❌ Cons: Strict combat timing requirements can feel exhausting for some, linear world exploration with limited traversal options, lack of a minimap and minor visual lip-sync bugs.
🏆Rating: 8.8 / 10

Unique and breath-taking visuals, story, music, characters, voice acting and dialogue. One of the most unique games I've played and it's very clear it was developed with a lot of passion and love, which is very rare to find nowadays.
Some minor gripes would be the somewhat confusing and hard to navigate UI, some parry timings being unintuitive and requiring strict memorisation, and some central lore pieces missing from the main story and available as a side content instead. All of these can be easily overcome by the player and this game remains a 9/10 must-play game for me.

supporting_evidence.quote:
RDR2 is a masterpiece in world-building, atmosphere, storytelling and immersion, which makes its controls all the more frustrating.

For a game so heavily focused on cinematic immersion, the clunky, sluggish and overly complicated controls constantly pull you out of the experience. Too many context-sensitive actions, too much input delay, too much fighting the character instead of simply controlling him.

It’s still an incredible game, but Rockstar’s refusal to properly adapt the controls for PC is a baffling design failure. Such a shame

I wanted to love this game. The game does have a lot of improvements over the last RCT for PC. But it's just badly executed. The camera controls are clunky and the game itself is an unstable buggy mess.

This is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ rip off cashing on the reputation of the franchise. It's just bad.

The developers are aware that using piece by piece building or editing roller coasters will crash the game randomly. They've been aware of the issue since 2017 and never released a patch to fix it.

This game would be decent if it was playable, it's not.

Get Planet Coaster instead, THAT is the game you're looking for.

Roller Coaster Tycoon World is buggy, clunky, and completely misses the charm of the classic games. The graphics feel outdated, the controls fight you, and the guests wander around like they’re lost. Even basic coaster building is a chore.

If you want the real theme-park tycoon experience, play literally any other entry in the series. Roller Coaster Tycoon World is the ride you skip so you can go get a pretzel instead.

don't hate me for this, but I didn't like the first Hades.
HOWEVER Hades II has totally won me over and blown me away.

supporting_evidence.quote:
Honestly, after waiting for what felt like forever, stepping into Pharloom as Hornet was worth every single second. I’m definitely not the most skilled gamer out there I died way more times than I’d like to admit but Hollow Knight: Silksong is an absolute masterpiece.

The movement feels so fluid and acrobatic compared to the original. Jumping, sprinting, and using Hornet’s needle craft makes combat feel like a fast-paced dance. The handcrafted art style, atmospheric music, and intricate world design continually blew me away. Every new area had me completely immersed, even when a brutal boss had me stuck for an hour.

It’s tough, but every victory feels earned and ridiculously satisfying. If you enjoy action platformers, atmospheric worlds, or just a really solid challenge, I can't recommend this game enough. Do yourself a favor and give it a play you won't regret it!

I won't lie, the day Silksong released I was sceptical and after about a week or 2 I stopped playing it entirely, until recently. I picked it up after "feeling bad that I havn't finished it when I loved Hollow Knight so much", so I naturally gave it another shot. I'm so glad I did. Sure, its different than Hollow Knight, but when you've adapted to the game it feels so good, from the combat down to every movement ability there is. The ending feels satisfying but also makes you want more.

10/10 would recommend

High quality game, combat, music, visuals 100/100 pure gold. Thank you devs. The way you character moves, it have weight and physics, inertia, mount riding too. Combat once you git gud is so satisfying and so addictive, I'm playing gs, aiming with focus made gs better. Music is epic in important boss fights, visuals and design too.
Cons.
Facial animations, eyes are frozen, played mhw after baldurs gate 3, so contrast in acting scenes were strong.
Dialoges and story so simple and positive so sterilized, I like it, but if it have real story plot it would be even better game.
Also high spec PC must have. I've played all high, ultra textures, game was smooth, haven't seen any issues, glitches or bugs. Took 18 hour to beat low rank and complete main story.

I loved RE7. RE8, however, was massively overhyped. Thankfully, RE9 is a return to form.

Let's start with the positives.

+It looks great.
+Runs well and is properly optimised.
+Crunchier, more satisfying combat with much better weapon sounds.
+More memorable than RE8, with stronger writing.
+An overall far more enjoyable experience than RE8.

Now the negatives.

-Grace's voice acting gets annoying with her constant stammering.
-Leon's voice actor sounds bored at times, although I suppose that's just part of his badass persona?
-Nerfed dismemberment compared to previous games.
-Still no f*****g FOV slider. Seriously, Capcom?

Overall, RE9 is a massive improvement over RE8. Better combat, better presentation, better writing, and a much more memorable experience. It's not perfect, but Capcom cooked - mostly.

query: How does PAYDAY 3 run on PC?
draft_reference_summary: PAYDAY 3 receives positive PC-performance feedback, including a highly upvoted review praising how well it runs and how polished it feels, while another account reports particularly strong performance after an engine upgrade.

draft_claims.text: PAYDAY 3 receives positive PC-performance feedback, including a highly upvoted review praising how well it runs and how polished it feels, while another account reports particularly strong performance after an engine upgrade.
draft_claims.text_zh: PAYDAY 3 的 PC 运行表现获得积极反馈，高赞评论肯定了运行状态和打磨程度，另有体验表示，引擎升级后性能尤其出色。

supporting_evidence.quote:
Credit where credit is due because Payday 3 has had such a turnaround from when it released.

It brings all the adrenaline and edge of your seat action of Payday 2 with EXTREMELY satisfying gunplay. It looks beautiful, it runs well, it's polished, the difficulty is rewarding, the music is brilliant, stealth is miles above PD2 in terms of complexity. And the talents and level reworks they've been doing have hit the sweet spot.

It feels unfair to compare the amount of content in this to its predecessor, when 2 has a solid 10 years worth of releases over Payday 3.

For a game that's been out nearly 3 years and had a rocky start, it's in a good place right now.

Honestly, I wouldn't compare this game to payday 2 that much, whilst it is based on it, it's frankly far different in how the gameplay goes, only negative thing I will say is that after these two and a half years (still counting) the game still lacks content, masks guns, heists and other stuff. I'm sure it will grow eventually, people have to let go of the terrible launch and just give this game a go. It won't leave you dissapointed if you don't expect a better graphics payday 2, also its well optimised, graphics are pretty good but my mid pc can still run it perfectly fine on ultras.

Genuinely quite good nowadays. Had a deservedly poor reputation when first released but after many revisions the game is actually quite a lot of fun now and worth picking up. The revised stealth mechanics alone make Payday 2 difficult to return to at times. Gunplay is much improved and all the new animations for interacting with drills, opening elevator shafts, etc. are neat touches. The game runs extremely well after the most recent engine upgrade and the upcoming crimebonds have some OK potential in exchange for free heists.

The skill trees are still quite boring unfortunately and there the main menu UI generally isn't great, particularly with the addition of crimebonds. Purchasing heist favours could do with being similar to Payday 2, rather than tucked away at the bottom of a vendor menu.

Payday 3 has a lot of potential. We certainly understand that the devs want to bring their own identity to the game, but there's no denying that many futures and lessons learned from Payday 2 would be great for the third installment:

-the police carrying the bags away (yes, it was annoying, but it was an extra challenge).

10/10 One of the best gaming experiences I’ve ever had.

Red Dead Redemption 2 is honestly on another level. The open world is absolutely incredible every place feels alive, every little detail feels intentional, and there’s always something new to discover. The story, characters, music, atmosphere, everything comes together so perfectly.

The game offers such deep immersion that I lose track of missions while simply exploring the detailed urban environment.

Highlights: A living open world, visual and audio details that capture your attention at every turn.
Freedom of exploration, wandering aimlessly becomes more appealing than following the main storyline to me.
High graphical demands, requires a powerful computer to run with maximum quality and fluidity.

Highly recommended if you have a good PC to play it properly.

There are things that this game does well too: amazing graphics, chsrming ambiance and top tier music.
Overall tho the experiance is lacking compared to the hype.

query: Is Resident Evil Resistance stable, or does it have technical issues?
draft_reference_summary: Resident Evil Resistance has match-disrupting problems: a highly upvoted review describes door-frame zombie exploits that block rooms and prevent completion, alongside cheating programs that undermine normal play and progression.

draft_claims.text: Resident Evil Resistance has match-disrupting problems: a highly upvoted review describes door-frame zombie exploits that block rooms and prevent completion, alongside cheating programs that undermine normal play and progression.
draft_claims.text_zh: Resident Evil Resistance 存在会破坏对局的问题：一条高赞评论批评了利用门框丧尸堵住房间、导致无法完成对局的漏洞，以及妨碍正常游玩和成长进度的作弊程序。

supporting_evidence.quote:
If you're going to be charging us full price for this game and still have the gall to charge $30 for 50 boosts, we deserve dedicated servers. Not having Masterminds host games where most high leveled Masterminds glitch rooms if they honestly felt like it.

(Edit: Resistance is included with RE3, but you're still paying full regardless. Can't say you paid $60 for RE3 and got Resistance for free. That's not the case.)

(Edit 2: Masterminds have made it a habit to lock survivors out of rooms by glitching zombies inbetween door frames, making them unkillable and leaving your group unable to finish the experiment. Since the inital review there have been worse cheaters. The use of Cheat Engine and other programs have made progression and regular gameplay either near impossible or just laughable.)

fixed_context.text:
Resident Evil Resistance is a really promising concept ! Taking the asymmetrical multiplayer idea of Dead by Daylight and putting it in the Resident Evil universe was such a cool move! The atmosphere, characters, and setting fit perfectly with this kind of gameplay.

...

That said, there are some downsides that really hurt the experience : long waiting times to find a match, a pretty limited map selection ; and maybe less of a dealbreaker but still noticeable : unbalanced teams. It can make matches feel a bit... chaotic, to say the least.

*Resident Evil: Resistance* has a fun idea with its 4v1 survival setup, but it never fully delivers. Matches can feel unbalanced, and the gameplay gets repetitive. My favorite part? Pulling off a clutch escape with the team—it’s chaotic fun when it works.

⭐☆☆☆☆

"Resident Evil Resistance is such a disappointment. The matchmaking is terrible, the balance between survivors and masterminds feels completely off, and the gameplay just isn’t fun. I kept hoping it would improve, but it never did—definitely not worth the time."

(Coming for someone returning to the game after seeing DLC vids)

They have fixed most performance issues. After playing with settings, I can easily get above 60 fps in most towns and during fights.

With Frame gen auto, I can get 90 - 100+ with out any issues in mouse responsiveness. Have gotten no crashes sense returning as well, and online play seems very stable.

Mind you this is with MY settings preference, You might want something on high that I have on low that tanks your fps.

TLDR; Performance issues mostly fixed, don't be poor and play with setting.

RE:RESISTANCE started off as a fairly interesting concept, but CAPCOM decided to discontinue support for it a few months after its release. At the time of writing this review, it is a half-dead, unbalanced game with an average of around 100 online players.

For achievement hunters: you’ll probably need to find a boosting group if you want to unlock all the achievements.

In my opinion, I think the Resident Evil team at Capcom should have focused more on the development of the Resident Evil 3 remake instead of this half-baked / rushed PvP game mode that came with it. The core mechanics and gameplay of this game tries to capture the same audience of other survival horror PvP games but there various issues that sets this game back. However, if you have a group of friends to play with, this could be potentially somewhat enjoyable.

If you're going to be charging us full price for this game and still have the gall to charge $30 for 50 boosts, we deserve dedicated servers. Not having Masterminds host games where most high leveled Masterminds glitch rooms if they honestly felt like it.

(Edit: Resistance is included with RE3, but you're still paying full regardless. Can't say you paid $60 for RE3 and got Resistance for free. That's not the case.)

(Edit 2: Masterminds have made it a habit to lock survivors out of rooms by glitching zombies inbetween door frames, making them unkillable and leaving your group unable to finish the experiment. Since the inital review there have been worse cheaters. The use of Cheat Engine and other programs have made progression and regular gameplay either near impossible or just laughable.)

Sure it has its flaws, but its a very fun game once you ignore its flaws. I dont have any problems with it, i can get 60fps on my 2070 super with the right settings. hopefully with more time the game becomes more optimized and less buggy.

Capcom had a good idea, it looked like we finally got a solid RE multiplayer. But then balancing issues hit, and that was it. Back to square one, waiting for a good RE multiplayer again. At this point, it’s hard not to think that RE should just stick to single player.

Well done Capcom!! The RE Engine gets better with every Resident Evil. Liking Grace she really sales the terror of horror. Angela Sant'Albano voice actress for Grace Ashcroft did an outstanding job capturing the paralyzing fear with in the Rhodes Hill Chronic Care Center. Gameplay gets better with each installment as well.It is a slightly reboot in my opinion.

supporting_evidence.quote:

fixed_context.text:
Double Fine slapped a "1.0" sticker on this game and abandoned it. Whilst I appreciate that there are times that an Early Access game may not deliver all of the promised features, this game received a small fraction of those features proposed.

But this is a game review, not a review of Double Fine's business practices. So how is the game?

In short, the game is a mess of buggy AI with barely enough gameplay mechanics to sustain more than a couple of hours of play. The character morale system is horribly half-baked, and the game is little more than a series of repetitive busywork tasks.

That Double Fine now has it's greasy mitts out for Early Access funding for Massive Chalice barely a month after abandoning DF-9 is an insult to all of those people who put their faith in the company.

Never again.

Honestly, after waiting for what felt like forever, stepping into Pharloom as Hornet was worth every single second. I’m definitely not the most skilled gamer out there I died way more times than I’d like to admit but Hollow Knight: Silksong is an absolute masterpiece.

The movement feels so fluid and acrobatic compared to the original. Jumping, sprinting, and using Hornet’s needle craft makes combat feel like a fast-paced dance. The handcrafted art style, atmospheric music, and intricate world design continually blew me away. Every new area had me completely immersed, even when a brutal boss had me stuck for an hour.

It’s tough, but every victory feels earned and ridiculously satisfying. If you enjoy action platformers, atmospheric worlds, or just a really solid challenge, I can't recommend this game enough. Do yourself a favor and give it a play you won't regret it!

The gameplay is equally impressive. Many boss fights feel like a dance as you weave in attacks and spells while dodging each strike. Having 100%ed this game and explored every corner of its world, I can’t recommend it highly enough to anyone looking for a rewarding time sink.

Fantastic game.
Even though I personally enjoyed the first Hollow Knight game a bit more, Silksong was still such an amazing experience.

If you want a beautiful Metroidvania then both Hollow Knight games are the perfect choice.

supporting_evidence.quote:
Honestly, after waiting for what felt like forever, stepping into Pharloom as Hornet was worth every single second. I’m definitely not the most skilled gamer out there I died way more times than I’d like to admit but Hollow Knight: Silksong is an absolute masterpiece.

The movement feels so fluid and acrobatic compared to the original. Jumping, sprinting, and using Hornet’s needle craft makes combat feel like a fast-paced dance. The handcrafted art style, atmospheric music, and intricate world design continually blew me away. Every new area had me completely immersed, even when a brutal boss had me stuck for an hour.

It’s tough, but every victory feels earned and ridiculously satisfying. If you enjoy action platformers, atmospheric worlds, or just a really solid challenge, I can't recommend this game enough. Do yourself a favor and give it a play you won't regret it!

I'm not saying this lightly, but I just cannot recommend this game. It's hard and tedious instead of hard but fun, unlike the previous installment. Underrewarding and constantly demanding, without ever giving you a break to explore the gorgeous world. It has its merits of course - graphics are lovely and detailed, music is beutiful and adds to the atmosphere, but I'm stating the obvious here. However, when the game frustrates me way more than it gives me satisfaction or a sense of wonder, then I'm afraid I'm done with the game. And Silksong happily shows me a middle finger at every step. As a Hollow Knight fan, I am disappointed. I wanted to love this game, but it simply wouldn't let me.
Say "skill issue" or whatever, I don't care.

Wilds might be one of my top games of all time. Again I'm not a long time fan of the franchise, but from the games I have played, Wilds just feels like the most polished vision of Monster Hunter while working within the confines of the RE Engine.

Graphically, it's beautiful, and I'm very aware that I'm fortunate enough to have experienced the game after a year of patches and QoL changes, even now I have to use frame generation to sit comfortably in the triple digit FPS range.

Despite that, I really liked the story with the Guardian monsters, and just subtle elements like bows having infinite arrow coatings was really nice as a bow main. That said, wasn't a fan of the insect glaive's handling of the kinsect gauges.

Very excited for Ascendance.

Fighting big monsters have never been more fun. Despite the rocky launch of this game I stuck with it for my love of the franchise, and I am very happy that with the updates past the base game has fixed so much of the performance and bugs in the game. Though my only gripe about MHWilds is how unstable some of the lobbies are sometimes I get dced from online play while other times it never happens just a lil shotty

The gameplay is fun, albeit somewhat easy for people familiar with the mechanics, and the monster roster is very good. My biggest issues are that most high-level endgame gear is locked behind RNG mechanics that lack a sense of measurable progress which makes grinding feel pointless and the streamlining of out-of-hunt and exploration mechanics makes the gameplay less impactful because it feels like a constant race to the next combat encounter. Compared to the previous titles on PC, this one is fun, but feels like a downgrade in all the areas that give Monster Hunter it's identity.

The music, art direction, and gameplay are peak imo. Some of the most fun I've had playing with friends (we're all big Monster Hunter fans since World/Iceborne).

I love the ecology/speculative evolution aspect of the Monster Hunter games, and it feels like they really fleshed that out here. The environments and ecosystems feel alive and it's beautiful.

The 2 path variety adds just enough of a break/change to the core gameplay loop to keep it interesting. Most of the challenges are fair and rewarding, and each of the weapons is distinct enough that having to do a run with each doesn't feel like an enormous slog.

The visuals and sound design is fantastic, and the music is a fantastic cherry on top.
This was my first MH game, and I love it. Lots of fun with friends and amazing character creation, maps, and cutscenes. Just wish we had less serious voice options.

query: Why do players say Hollow Knight's controls feel tight and responsive?
draft_reference_summary: Hollow Knight's controls feel tight because actions respond closely to player input and support smooth combat, with simple controller operation adding to the sense of responsiveness.

draft_claims.text: Hollow Knight's controls feel tight because actions respond closely to player input and support smooth combat, with simple controller operation adding to the sense of responsiveness.
draft_claims.text_zh: Hollow Knight 的操作之所以显得精准，在于动作能够贴近玩家输入、战斗衔接流畅；手柄操作的简洁性，也增强了这种反应灵敏的体验。

supporting_evidence.quote:
Hollow Knight is not just a game; it is a descent into a haunting, melancholic dream.

Team Cherry didn't just build a world; they unearthed a vast, forgotten kingdom. Hallownest is a masterclass in atmospheric storytelling, where every rain-soaked ruin in the City of Tears and every shadow in Deepnest echoes with lost glory, backed by Christopher Larkin’s achingly gorgeous score.

The gameplay is surgical perfection. Tight, responsive controls, the hypnotic satisfaction of nail-pogoing, and boss fights that demand absolute respect and rhythm. You get lost, you adapt, you overcome.

An untouchable monument of the Metroidvania genre and an absolute work of art. 10/10.

Absolute Masterpiece! (9/10)
​Hollow Knight is a breathtaking journey through a beautifully dark and tragic world. Everything in this game comes together perfectly to create an unforgettable experience:
​Gameplay & Combat: Silky-smooth mechanics, tight controls, and rewarding progression.
​Music & Atmosphere: The soundtrack and visual design are hauntingly beautiful, drawing you deep into the lore of Hallownest.
​Challenge: The difficulty is tough and demanding, but incredibly satisfying to master.
​Final Score: 9 / 10
The only reason it’s not a full 10/10 is the lack of official Arabic lauage support. Other than that, it is near perfection. Highly recommended to anyone who loves Metroidvanias and great storytelling!

TIGHT controls. The controller truly feels like an extension of your body in this game. You learn to love the pain of trial and error, and after awhile you'll be surprised that you're even capable of doing the things you're watching yourself do on the screen. Some of the bosses in the very, very late parts of the game if you're trying to go for completion are ridiculously hard, though, so this game is not for the faint of heart.

Hollow knight is a great game and through out the 2 years of playing, its great. It kicks you off without knowing anything, simple controlls, expesaly on controllor. It has a amazing story, so lore deap charicters, and its amazing as a bullet easy to hell 2d platformer and great backtrack/areas, good sound tracks, and nice boss fights. also replayable with a charm (loadout) sistem. one thing... speedrun achivement.

Hollow Knight is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Its deeply immersive worldbuilding and masterful storytelling come together to create an unforgettable narrative. The phenomenal soundtrack also deserves every bit of praise it receives. Christopher Larkin was truly cooking, and many tracks have found their way into my everyday playlists.
The gameplay is equally impressive. Many boss fights feel like a dance as you weave in attacks and spells while dodging each strike. Having 100%ed this game and explored every corner of its world, I can’t recommend it highly enough to anyone looking for a rewarding time sink.

This game improves on hollow knight. The sound track is amazing, the movement is smooth and fast paced, the combat is awesome. It's a really good game except for some of the runbacks and places such as bilewater is a pain in the ass. You really have to be passionate about the hollow knight universe to really enjoy this game. As someone who is really passionate about Hollow Knight (Reached to the top of P5), this game felt natural. The bosses were not too difficult since I am used to the movement and seeing openings etc. But I can see a person completely new to hollow knight suffer with the past faced gameplay and double heart damage. I would really suggest playing Hollow Knight first and then picking this game up. If u already beat Hollow Knight, this game is a must play.

Honestly, after waiting for what felt like forever, stepping into Pharloom as Hornet was worth every single second. I’m definitely not the most skilled gamer out there I died way more times than I’d like to admit but Hollow Knight: Silksong is an absolute masterpiece.

The movement feels so fluid and acrobatic compared to the original. Jumping, sprinting, and using Hornet’s needle craft makes combat feel like a fast-paced dance. The handcrafted art style, atmospheric music, and intricate world design continually blew me away. Every new area had me completely immersed, even when a brutal boss had me stuck for an hour.

It’s tough, but every victory feels earned and ridiculously satisfying. If you enjoy action platformers, atmospheric worlds, or just a really solid challenge, I can't recommend this game enough. Do yourself a favor and give it a play you won't regret it!

The story is gripping and quite engrossing, and the gameplay is engaging. The interaction of the various systems - netrunning, guns, melee, stealth - allow for many different types of characters. The controls - responsive. The characters - quite memorable. There are a few bugs, but nothing that can't be resolved by a quick save/reload, and certainly nothing gamebreaking.

As someone who loved Hollow Knight, I can't help but just adore Silksong.
Hornet's movement definitely took a while to get a hang of, but once you get it you get it. Going back to Hollow Knight afterwards just makes the Knight's gameplay feel so clunky (I STILL LOVE HOLLOW KNIGHT).
I would say that Hollow Knight is definitely 'required reading' before playing Silksong from a story and gamplay perspective.

Genuinely such an amazing game that you can tell had so much love and effort put into it.

i love hollow knight silksong, its such a beautiful game and its smooth and fun to play (especially with controller) the new world looks so great and fascinating in the game and the entire game itself is a major upgrade from the previous hollow knight!

supporting_evidence.quote:
Thoroughly enjoyed Cyberpunk 2077. I chose to purchase it well after the bugs and customer complaints which were coming out during its initial release, meaning I've had minimal issues.

Interesting storyline, fun side quests/missions, some in-depth characters and a strong performance from Keanu Reeves. As someone who loves character customisation, this game allows for some pretty fantastic outfit, hair, makeup, facial feature and weapon options.

Some of the missions do become repetitive, though many can be skipped or passed on if you're just interested in the main storyline (still want to make sure to build you stats though and connect with a few key characters...).

I recommend this, especially if you're a fan of futuristic, dystopian cities and challenging morals.

query: Is Resident Evil Resistance balanced, and does it work without technical problems?
draft_reference_summary: Resident Evil Resistance's balance is criticized as uneven between survivors and masterminds, with long matchmaking waits and a diminished population adding to the friction. A highly upvoted review describes door-blocking zombie exploits and cheating programs that disrupt play. Successful coordinated escapes can still be fun, but do not remove the imbalance or repetition.

draft_claims.text: Resident Evil Resistance's balance is criticized as uneven between survivors and masterminds, with long matchmaking waits and a diminished population adding to the friction.
draft_claims.text_zh: Resident Evil Resistance 的幸存者与操纵者之间存在失衡，较长的匹配等待和减少的玩家人数，又增加了游玩阻力。

supporting_evidence.quote:
⭐☆☆☆☆

"Resident Evil Resistance is such a disappointment. The matchmaking is terrible, the balance between survivors and masterminds feels completely off, and the gameplay just isn’t fun. I kept hoping it would improve, but it never did—definitely not worth the time."

Resident Evil Resistance is a really promising concept ! Taking the asymmetrical multiplayer idea of Dead by Daylight and putting it in the Resident Evil universe was such a cool move! The atmosphere, characters, and setting fit perfectly with this kind of gameplay.

...

That said, there are some downsides that really hurt the experience : long waiting times to find a match, a pretty limited map selection ; and maybe less of a dealbreaker but still noticeable : unbalanced teams. It can make matches feel a bit... chaotic, to say the least.

RE:RESISTANCE started off as a fairly interesting concept, but CAPCOM decided to discontinue support for it a few months after its release. At the time of writing this review, it is a half-dead, unbalanced game with an average of around 100 online players.

For achievement hunters: you’ll probably need to find a boosting group if you want to unlock all the achievements.

Capcom had a good idea, it looked like we finally got a solid RE multiplayer. But then balancing issues hit, and that was it. Back to square one, waiting for a good RE multiplayer again. At this point, it’s hard not to think that RE should just stick to single player.

draft_claims.text: A highly upvoted review describes door-blocking zombie exploits and cheating programs that disrupt play.
draft_claims.text_zh: 一条高赞评论还批评了利用丧尸堵门的漏洞，以及破坏体验的作弊程序。

supporting_evidence.quote:
If you're going to be charging us full price for this game and still have the gall to charge $30 for 50 boosts, we deserve dedicated servers. Not having Masterminds host games where most high leveled Masterminds glitch rooms if they honestly felt like it.

(Edit: Resistance is included with RE3, but you're still paying full regardless. Can't say you paid $60 for RE3 and got Resistance for free. That's not the case.)

(Edit 2: Masterminds have made it a habit to lock survivors out of rooms by glitching zombies inbetween door frames, making them unkillable and leaving your group unable to finish the experiment. Since the inital review there have been worse cheaters. The use of Cheat Engine and other programs have made progression and regular gameplay either near impossible or just laughable.)

It runs silky smooth at 100+ FPS, gunplay feels phenomenal, and the climax delivers in every way possible.

Capcom knocked it out of the park. If you love Resident Evil, this is an essential buy.

fixed_context.text:
I loved RE7. RE8, however, was massively overhyped. Thankfully, RE9 is a return to form.

Let's start with the positives.

+It looks great.
+Runs well and is properly optimised.
+Crunchier, more satisfying combat with much better weapon sounds.
+More memorable than RE8, with stronger writing.
+An overall far more enjoyable experience than RE8.

Now the negatives.

-Grace's voice acting gets annoying with her constant stammering.
-Leon's voice actor sounds bored at times, although I suppose that's just part of his badass persona?
-Nerfed dismemberment compared to previous games.
-Still no f*****g FOV slider. Seriously, Capcom?

Overall, RE9 is a massive improvement over RE8. Better combat, better presentation, better writing, and a much more memorable experience. It's not perfect, but Capcom cooked - mostly.

query_zh: 哪些游戏优化好、运行流畅？

legacy_drafts.en: Resident Evil Requiem reviewers report smooth PC performance, including 1440p on a five-year-old PC and a separate report above 100 FPS; Left 4 Dead 2 is also praised for broad hardware compatibility and optimization. Cyberpunk 2077 receives smooth-performance reports on Linux and, separately, a full AMD setup in 2026, while one Monster Hunter Wilds reviewer reports good performance after an optimization update. Other supplied examples include Red Dead Redemption 2 running smoothly without frame generation and GTA V Legacy running well on a reviewer's PC.
legacy_drafts.zh: Resident Evil Requiem 评论者报告 PC 运行流畅，包括五年旧 PC 上的 1440p 体验，以及另一人超过 100 FPS 的报告；Left 4 Dead 2 也因广泛的硬件适应性和优化受到称赞。Cyberpunk 2077 有 Linux 上流畅运行的报告，另有一位在 2026 年使用全 AMD 配置的玩家表示运行流畅；一位 Monster Hunter Wilds 评论者则表示优化更新后性能良好。其他例子包括不使用帧生成也能流畅运行的 Red Dead Redemption 2，以及在一位评论者 PC 上运行良好的 GTA V Legacy。

legacy_drafts.en: Two Resident Evil Requiem reviews with 1 helpful vote each report smooth 1440p play on a five-year-old PC and performance above 100 FPS, respectively; Left 4 Dead 2 is also praised for broad hardware compatibility and optimization. Cyberpunk 2077 receives smooth-performance reports on Linux and, separately, a full AMD setup in 2026, while one Monster Hunter Wilds reviewer reports good performance after an optimization update. Other supplied examples include Red Dead Redemption 2 running smoothly without frame generation and GTA V Legacy running well on a reviewer's PC.
legacy_drafts.zh: 两条各获 1 次有用投票的 Resident Evil Requiem 评论分别报告，在使用五年的 PC 上可以流畅运行 1440p，以及帧率超过 100 FPS；Left 4 Dead 2 也因广泛的硬件适应性和优化受到称赞。Cyberpunk 2077 有 Linux 上流畅运行的报告，另有一位在 2026 年使用全 AMD 配置的玩家表示运行流畅；一位 Monster Hunter Wilds 评论者则表示优化更新后性能良好。其他例子包括不使用帧生成也能流畅运行的 Red Dead Redemption 2，以及在一位评论者 PC 上运行良好的 GTA V Legacy。
